title: BrandonMYates/schwarzschild-comparator
abstract: Twenty-one theorems and thirty-three definitions, machine-checked in Lean 4 against Mathlib v4.32.0: the Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Kottler), Reissner-Nordstrom (with the Maxwell stress tensor defined and G = 8 pi T proved in all sixteen components), ingoing Vaidya (null dust of rank at most one, rank one wherever dm/dv ≠ 0, for a merely once-differentiable mass function), spatially flat FLRW (both Friedmann equations in Einstein-tensor form), static de Sitter, Minkowski-in-spherical and Kiselev metrics, together with Birkhoff uniqueness in the areal static gauge and the n != 2 equivalence of the two forms of the vacuum equations. The results are classical and NO NEW MATHEMATICS IS CLAIMED: this is a proof of concept for the definitions. Lean checks that a proof establishes a statement, not that a definition means what its name says, so the entry certifies its sign, index and contraction conventions by computing textbook solutions with them -- including four NONZERO answers (de Sitter R = 12/L^2, Reissner-Nordstrom R_thetatheta = Q^2/r^2, Vaidya R_vv = 2 (dm/dv)/r^2, Kiselev R_thetatheta = -3wc r^-(3w+1)), because a curvature definition that was accidentally identically zero would still prove every vacuum theorem here. Scope: everything is a computation in ONE FIXED CHART, an open subset of R^4 -- no atlas, no manifold, no coordinate-independence theorem, no maximal extension, and horizons and coordinate poles lie outside every statement. NOT compared: Ricci symmetry R_bd = R_db in general (it needs Clairaut for the coordinate partial derivative, which Mathlib supplies only for fderiv) or the Bianchi identities; Maxwell's own equations; any matter model, fluid or energy condition beyond the single defined Maxwell stress tensor; non-flat FLRW; the outgoing Vaidya chart. Audience: general relativists, for whom this is the definitional layer a junction-condition or thin-shell statement would be written against, and the formalization community, for whom it is coverage-creating rather than coverage-duplicating. Mathlib v4.32.0 contains no curvature of any kind -- christoffel, ricci, scalarCurvature, Lorentzian, PseudoRiemannian and five further names return zero hits across all 8,264 .lean files at the pinned revision, and its one metric structure hard-codes positive definiteness -- so the entire chain is defined inline in the Challenge.
